summary: A 1913 Conservation Commission station on Tooley Pond Mountain; its steel tower came down in 1971 and was re-erected on Cathedral Rock.

facts.status_note: No tower stands on Tooley Pond Mountain. The steel tower was taken down in 1971 and re-erected on Cathedral Rock.

visit.trail_note: A marked trail up Tooley Mountain starts from a parking area by Tooley Pond; no tower stands there.

events.note: Wooden station built by the Conservation Commission; R.W. Higbie Lumber Company paid for the material for the tower, cabin and lines
Station not staffed in its first season
Wooden station replaced by a steel 47-foot Aermotor LS40 tower
Ralph Cole of DeKalb Junction to take over the fire tower, per the Syracuse Herald Journal
Lookout operations ended at the close of the 1971 season
Taken down from Tooley Pond Mountain by SUNY-ESF students at Wanakena
Ranger School classes were erecting an old fire tower on Cathedral Rock by February 1982, per a Tribune-Press item quoted by Forest Lookouts
Cab finished in 1999 per Wikipedia; the register dates the re-erection to the late 1990s
Windows and final restorations complete; dedicated July 2000 per Wikipedia
Cathedral Rock tower registered December 23, 2022 as US 1698, NY 50

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia's lead gives 1919 for the first tower on the mountain, but its history section and the 1913 Conservation Commission report describe a wooden station in 1913 and the steel tower in 1919. The 1913 date is used here.

Sources disagree on when the tower was re-erected at Cathedral Rock. A February 1982 newspaper item shows classes erecting it; Wikipedia gives the 1980s start, a 1999 cab and a 2000 dedication; the register says late 1990s.

sources.title: Hikes, climbs along historic Tooley Pond Road

notes_for_editor: This record is the original site. The Cathedral Rock tower already has its own story and research file under us-ny-tooley-pond-mountain-at-cathedral-rock; the two overlap on the rebuild. Wikipedia's lead (1919) conflicts with its own history section (1913); the 1913 date follows the Conservation Commission report. The rebuild dates disagree across sources. No fresh photos found.
